In the year to 30 June 2026 it created a mortgage over its Gurugram premises in favour of an Indian bank, painted a new signboard outside those premises bearing only the words 'Kestrel Analytics', and decided in principle to close its Indian place of business in 2027. Its accounts for the Indian business operations have been audited by a practising chartered accountant in India.

readLink.label: Read: A compliance timeline for a foreign company →

questions.stem: For the financial year ended 30 June 2026, the last date for filing the annual return of Kestrel Analytics Inc with the Registrar is:
questions.sourceRef: Companies Act 2013, s. 384(2) read with the Companies (Registration of Foreign Companies) Rules 2014 — sixty days from the last day of the financial year

options.text: 29 August 2026
options.explanation: Correct. Sixty days from 30 June 2026: July supplies 31 days, taking the count to 31 on 31 July, and the remaining 29 days run into August.

options.text: 30 August 2026
options.explanation: That reads sixty days as two calendar months. July's 31 days make the day-count and the month-count differ by one.

options.text: 30 July 2026
options.explanation: That is thirty days — the section 380 period, which runs from the establishment of a place of business or from an alteration in the notified particulars.

options.text: 30 December 2026
options.explanation: That is six months, which is the window for filing the FINANCIAL STATEMENTS, not the annual return.

questions.stem: As to the new signboard bearing only the words 'Kestrel Analytics', the position under section 382 is that:

options.text: It complies, because the company's name is displayed and the country of incorporation appears on its letterhead
options.explanation: The requirement in clause (a) is independent of the requirement in clause (b). The country of incorporation must appear on the signboard as well.

options.text: It does not comply: the display outside every place of business must show the name of the company AND the country in which it is incorporated, in legible English characters and also in the characters of a language in general use in that locality
options.explanation: Correct. Two defects — the country of incorporation is missing, and the local-language display required by section 382(a) is missing. Contravention attracts the fine in section 392.

options.text: It does not comply, because the signboard must also state the Corporate Identity Number of the company
options.explanation: A CIN is allotted under section 7(3) to a company incorporated in India. A foreign company has none, and section 382 does not ask for one.

options.text: Section 382 applies only to the principal place of business notified under section 380(1)(e)
options.explanation: Section 382(a) applies to EVERY office or place where the company carries on business in India, not only the principal one.

questions.stem: As to the mortgage of the Gurugram premises:

options.text: No registration is required, Chapter VI applying only to companies incorporated in India
options.explanation: Section 384(4) exists to extend Chapter VI to foreign companies for their Indian property.

options.text: Registration is required only if the mortgage exceeds a prescribed value
options.explanation: Chapter VI has no value threshold; the obligation attaches to the creation of the charge itself.

options.text: Disclosure of the premises in the list of places of business filed under section 381(4) is sufficient
options.explanation: That list discloses premises, not security. It has no bearing on the registration of charges.

options.text: Chapter VI applies mutatis mutandis, the property having been created or acquired in India, so the charge must be registered with the Registrar within thirty days of its creation, failing which it is void against the liquidator and other creditors
options.explanation: Correct. Section 384(4) applies Chapter VI to charges on properties created or acquired by a foreign company in India, carrying with it the thirty-day window under section 77(1), the extended windows on additional and ad valorem fees, and the consequence of non-registration.

questions.stem: When Kestrel Analytics Inc closes its Indian place of business in 2027, the applicable provision is:

options.text: Section 248, the company applying to the Registrar for removal of its name from the register of companies
options.explanation: Section 248 removes the name of a company registered in India from the register. A foreign company has no name on that register to remove.

options.text: Section 380(3), a return of the alteration being sufficient to record the closure
options.explanation: A section 380(3) return records an alteration in the notified particulars. The closure of the Indian place of business engages a separate and heavier provision.

options.text: Section 391(2): notwithstanding section 376, the provisions of Chapter XX (winding up) apply mutatis mutandis for the closure of the place of business of a foreign company in India, as if it were a company incorporated in India
options.explanation: Correct. Section 391(2), as substituted, applies the winding-up chapter to the closure of a foreign company's Indian place of business, and is not confined to companies that have issued a prospectus or Indian Depository Receipts here.

options.text: Section 393A, the Central Government notifying the closure
options.explanation: Section 393A is an exemption power exercisable in respect of classes of foreign companies. It has nothing to do with closure.
